extracted.intended_audience: general readers and Wikipedia editors interested in Joe Biden and U.S. political history
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic Wikipedia entry documenting Joe Biden's 1988 presidential campaign, its background, controversies (notably the Neil Kinnock plagiarism episode), withdrawal, and aftermath. The page includes editorial templates and hidden-category metadata about language, date format, and article-level maintenance notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive detail / spin off minute detail
rubrics_metrics.description: This section contains an excessive amount of intricate detail. Specifically, minute detail about campaign staff is unnecessary for a Wikipedia page about a presidential campaign that didn't even last until the primaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please help improve it by spinning off or relocating relevant information and removing excessive detail that goes against Wikipedia's inclusion policy. (January 2026) (Learn how and when to remove this message) — aimed at editors: remove unnecessary minutiae and consider creating separate articles or subsections for highly detailed material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use American English
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article is tagged to follow American English spelling and usage; editors should conform to that variety of English for consistency across the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mdy dates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates in the article should follow the month-day-year format (e.g., June 9, 1987) to match the project's conventions for this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address style issues flagged by maintenance templates
rubrics_metrics.description: The article is marked with maintenance/style issue categories and templates (e.g., 'Wikipedia articles with style issues', 'All articles with style issues').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should resolve the specific style issues indicated by templates—such as excessive detail, citation formatting, lead/lede structure, or other flagged problems—following Wikipedia's style guides and project norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good article classification (article-level quality standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page appears in the 'Good articles' category, indicating it meets (or is intended to meet) Wikipedia's Good Article criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If treated as a Good Article, the page should satisfy the Good Article criteria: well-written, verifiable with reliable sources, broad coverage of the topic without major omissions, neutral point of view, and consistent formatting and citations.
